query: My claim was denied. What's wrong with it?
rationale: Source of truth: data/claims.json (CLM-1001: DENIED/AUTH_REQUIRED, member M-1001, service MRI-KNEE, servicing PRV-1001, ordering PRV-4001); data/benefits.json (BEN-GOLD-MRI-KNEE: covered=true, requires_prior_auth=true); data/prior_authorizations.json (no record for M-1002... i.e. no record with member_id=M-1001, confirming zero matching authorizations). Policy sections chosen by reading documents/imaging_policy.md (IMG-2 directly states MRI needs prior auth), documents/prior_authorization_policy.md (PA-4 defines the AUTH_REQUIRED code), and documents/claims_denial_guide.md (CLM-2 is the denial-guide's own AUTH_REQUIRED entry) -- not by running the retriever.

query: Is there an approved authorization on file for this MRI?
rationale: Source of truth: data/prior_authorizations.json has exactly two records for member_id=M-1002 + service_code=MRI-KNEE -- PA-1501 (EXPIRED, 2025 window) and PA-2001 (APPROVED, 2026 window covering the claim's 2026-02-12 date of service). Both are expected as graph evidence (HAS_AUTHORIZATION x2), per the domain intent that a member's authorization HISTORY is visible, not just whichever record happens to be currently applicable -- that judgment belongs to a future reasoning layer, not this evidence layer. Policy sections: IMG-2 (MRI prior-auth requirement) and PA-3 (effective/expiration window concept, directly relevant to why two differently-dated records for the same member/service matter) chosen from reading the documents directly.

query: Why was my lab claim denied?
rationale: Source of truth: data/benefits.json has an explicit BEN-SILVER-LAB-BASIC record with covered=false -- this is an AUTHORITATIVE, PRESENT benefit determination, not an absence of data. benefit_present MUST be true here (deliberately distinct from Case 5, where no benefit record exists at all) -- 'benefit_present=true, benefit_covered=false' must never be collapsed into a 'benefit missing' classification. Policy sections BEN-3 (states LAB-BASIC is not covered under Silver) and CLM-3 (defines SERVICE_NOT_COVERED) chosen by reading documents/benefits_guide.md and documents/claims_denial_guide.md directly. prior_authorization is still expected as missing evidence: no PA record exists for M-1003 in data/prior_authorizations.json, and that absence is reported regardless of whether prior auth was ever relevant to this service (LAB-BASIC never requires it) -- the absence is a fact about retrieval, not a judgment about relevance.

query: Why was my physical therapy claim denied?
rationale: Source of truth: data/providers.json shows PRV-2002 (Sunrise Physical Therapy Group) as network_status=out-of-network with network_name=null -- it must be present as a Provider node (the claim really was serviced there) but must structurally have NO PARTICIPATES_IN edge, since it has no home network to participate in; this is the 'provider/network evidence reflects the out-of-network scenario' requirement, expressed as a forbidden relationship pattern rather than a positive expectation. The ordering provider PRV-4002 (Dr. Sam Rivera) IS on Meridian Silver Network per providers.json and should show that edge. Policy sections CLM-4 (defines OUT_OF_NETWORK_PROVIDER) and NET-3 (explains out-of-network consequences) chosen from documents/claims_denial_guide.md and documents/provider_network_policy.md directly.

query: Why was my specialist visit claim denied?
rationale: Source of truth: data/claims.json has denial_reason_code=null for CLM-1005 (must not be invented as any specific code); data/benefits.json has no record at all for plan_id=PLAN-BRONZE + service_code=SPECIALIST-VISIT (benefit_present=false, a genuine absence, unlike Case 3); data/providers.json has no record with provider_id=PRV-9999, the claim's own servicing provider_id -- that id must never appear anywhere in the graph, and no SERVICED_BY edge may exist for this claim at all (not even to a placeholder). Policy sections CLM-5 (Claims With Incomplete Information) and BEN-5 (When Benefit Information Is Missing) chosen because both documents directly describe this exact scenario -- missing rule, escalate, never assume -- read from documents/claims_denial_guide.md and documents/benefits_guide.md directly.
